THE FINDING: WE HAD MEASURED EXECUTION LOSS ON WINNERS AND NEVER ONCE ON LOSERS. _ratchet_slippage (08-26) proved the ratchet leaks +0.110R/arm because it arms AT market. The symmetric question -- did the ORIGINAL stop deliver the -1.00R it promised? -- was never asked, and EXIT MECHANISM cannot answer it: it pools all twelve original-stop exits into one meanR of -0.996, which is indistinguishable between twelve perfect fills and twelve that missed by +-0.2R in cancelling directions. Those two worlds imply opposite fixes. ADDED analyze._stop_fill_quality + a STOP FILL QUALITY report section. RESULT, and it is a clean NEGATIVE: n=12, net +0.047R, mean +0.0039R/stop, 6 filled adverse and 6 favourable. THE RESTING EXCHANGE STOP IS EXECUTION-UNBIASED. Per event the ratchet leaks 28x more. So execution loss in this book is a PLACEMENT problem (the ratchet rests its new stop on the price that just traded, so one adverse tick fires it) and NOT a venue/liquidity tax -- which retires the obvious next hypothesis before a session spends itself on tightening brackets. The verdict is printed in the report in those words so it is not re-derived. SECOND FINDING (why the dev column cannot be read alone): 1R spans 0.48%-4.37% of entry (9.1x) at a FIXED SL_ATR_MULT. FIL 08-12 lost 0.190R on a 0.092% miss; ARB 09-05 lost only 0.147R on a 0.614% miss -- 6.7x the miss, less of the damage. Slippage is priced in percent, edge is counted in R, and width_pct is the exchange rate. The section prints all three columns and the identity dev_r = -(adv_pct x trigger)/(width_pct x entry) is pinned by test.
